model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between the sparsity rate and the perplexity for two different methods: Per-Output and Per-Layer. The horizontal axis, labeled "Sparsity Rate," represents the percentage of sparsity ranging from 10% to 80%. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," is on a logarithmic scale, indicating the perplexity values. The Per-Output method is represented by blue bars, while the Per-Layer method is represented by orange bars. At 10% sparsity, both methods have a low perplexity, with Per-Output slightly lower than Per-Layer. As the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity for both methods also increases, with Per-Output consistently showing lower perplexity than Per-Layer. The most significant difference in perplexity is observed at 80% sparsity, where Per-Output has a much lower perplexity compared to Per-Layer. The bars are not sorted in any specific order, and there are no bars that are visually emphasized.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between the sparsity rate and the perplexity for two different methods: Per-Output and Per-Layer. The horizontal axis, labeled "Sparsity Rate," represents the percentage of sparsity ranging from 10% to 80%, with increments of 10%. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," is on a logarithmic scale, indicating the perplexity values, which range from 10^0 to 10^3. Each bar is color-coded, with blue representing Per-Output and orange representing Per-Layer. The bars are arranged in pairs for each sparsity rate, with the Per-Output method shown on the left and the Per-Layer method on the right. The bars increase in height as the sparsity rate increases, indicating that both methods experience an increase in perplexity with higher sparsity rates. The Per-Layer method consistently shows higher perplexity values than the Per-Output method across all sparsity rates. The chart does not include any bars that are sorted in a specific way or visually emphasized.
model_annotations.German: Die bargezeichnete Grafik veranschaulicht die Perplexität in Abhängigkeit von der Sparte Rate, wobei zwei Kategorien, Per-Output und Per-Layer, verglichen werden. Die x-Achse repräsentiert die Sparte Rate, die in Prozent angegeben ist, und reicht von 10% bis 80%, wobei die Werte in 10% Intervallen angeordnet sind. Die y-Achse zeigt die Perplexität, die logarithmisch skaliert ist, mit einem logarithmischen Skalierungsfaktor von 10. Die Perplexität reicht von 10^0 bis 10^3. Die Per-Output-Kategorie wird durch blaue Balken dargestellt, während die Per-Layer-Kategorie durch orangefarbene Balken dargestellt wird. Die Perplexität für Per-Output ist im Allgemeinen niedriger als für Per-Layer, insbesondere bei höheren Sparte Raten. Die Perplexität für Per-Output steigt mit der Sparte Rate, wobei sie bei 80% am höchsten ist, während die Perplexität für Per-Layer ebenfalls mit der Sparte Rate steigt, aber bei 80% am niedrigsten ist. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, und es gibt keine besonderen Hervorhebungen oder Anmerkungen.
